snippet.title: RIP TO MICHAEL JACKSON -  A TRUE HUMANITARIAN TO THE WORLD 🥺🥺💔💔🕊️🕊️
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s legacy extends far beyond his music; his philanthropic efforts, particularly for children, were deeply personal and a consistent part of his life. Wherever his global tours took him, he almost always incorporated visits to local hospitals and orphanages, bringing gifts, financial support, and a moment of joy to those who were suffering.

Here is a breakdown of how he contributed to children around the world through his visits and philanthropy.

Notable Hospital and Orphanage Visits
Throughout his career, Jackson made it a priority to bring comfort to sick and underprivileged children globally:
 
* Brotman Memorial Hospital (Los Angeles)
   1984
   After suffering second- and third-degree burns while filming a Pepsi commercial, Jackson was treated at Brotman Memorial Hospital. He subsequently donated his entire $1.5 million settlement from Pepsi to equip a 19-bed unit, which was renamed the "Michael Jackson Burn Center for Children."

 * Bambino Gesù & Great Ormond Street Hospitals (Europe)
   1988
   While on the Bad World Tour, Jackson visited the Bambino Gesù Children's Hospital in Rome, handing out sweets and records to cancer patients and pledging £100,000. Weeks later, he visited Great Ormond Street Hospital in London, spending time with terminally ill children and donating £300,000 to the facility.

 *African Tour & Sophia Children's Hospital
   1992
   In early 1992, Jackson traveled 30,000 miles across Africa over 11 days specifically to visit hospitals, orphanages, schools, and institutions for disabled children. Later that year, he visited Sophia Children's Hospital in Rotterdam, donating £100,000 to build the "Michael Jackson Playroom."

*Orphanages in Mexico and Eastern Europe
   1993 - 1996
   Jackson routinely visited orphanages. In 1993, he hosted children from a Mexico City orphanage at the Hard Rock Café and arranged a theme park visit for 5,000 underprivileged kids. During his HIStory World Tour in 1996, he spent time at orphanages in Tokyo, Prague, and Romania, famously stating his desire to help "heal our wounded world."

Behind the Scenes: A Concert Tradition
Jackson’s dedication wasn't limited to hospital wards. During his major world tours (Bad, Dangerous, and HIStory), he established a quiet tradition that allowed sick children to experience his shows. His vocal coach, Seth Riggs, recalled that Jackson would frequently arrange for terminally ill children to be brought to his concerts.
 "Every night the kids would come in on stretchers, so sick they could hardly hold their heads up. Michael would kneel down at the stretchers and put his face right down beside theirs so that he could have his picture taken with them... The kids would perk right up in his presence." — Seth Riggs

Individual Acts of Generosity
Beyond institutional donations, Jackson often provided direct financial and emotional support to individual children facing immense hardships:

Bela Farkas (Hungary, 1994): While visiting Bethesda Children’s Hospital in Budapest, Jackson met a 4-year-old boy named Bela who needed a life-saving liver transplant that his family could not afford. Jackson paid for the transplant and covered the boy's medical expenses for the next ten years.

Ryan White (USA, late 1980s): Jackson befriended Ryan White, a teenager who became a national poster child for HIV/AIDS after being expelled from middle school due to his infection. Jackson invited Ryan to spend holidays at Neverland Ranch, bought him a car, and provided emotional support until Ryan's passing in 1990. This highly publicized friendship helped push for the passage of the Ryan White CARE Act.

Three Young Orphans (Los Angeles, 1980s): Upon hearing from a realtor about three teenagers who were about to lose their home and be separated after the death of their elderly father, Jackson quietly stepped in. He secretly paid to stop the foreclosure, covered their father's funeral expenses, arranged for a larger apartment for them to live with a relative, and provided scholarships for them to attend college.

The Heal the World Foundation
In 1992, Jackson formalized his philanthropic efforts by founding the Heal the World Foundation. The organization provided medicine to children in war-torn Sarajevo, funded drug abuse education, and airlifted millions of dollars in supplies to children worldwide. He famously donated all of his personal profits from the Dangerous World Tour—amounting to millions of dollars—directly to the foundation and other related charities.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON & DIANA ROSS LIVE - ROCK WITH YOU - February 05th 1981
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson and Diana Ross performed a legendary live duet of "Rock With You" for Diana Ross's CBS television special, simply titled diana.
Here are the key dates and details of the performance:

Filming Date: 
The live concert portion of the special was filmed on February 5, 1981, at The Forum in Los Angeles, California.
Air Date: The special was broadcast to the public on March 2, 1981.

Behind the Performance
The diana TV special was designed to capitalize on the massive success of her 1980 album of the same name (which featured the hit "Upside Down"). Because of their incredibly close relationship—having met years earlier when Motown introduced the Jackson 5 to the world—Michael was a natural choice as a guest star.
During the concert segment, Diana called Michael up to the stage. They first danced and sang to her chart-topping hit "Upside Down" before smoothly transitioning into a duet of his 1979 hit "Rock With You" from the Off the Wall album.

Memorable Moments:
The Chemistry:Their dynamic on stage was incredibly warm and playful. At one point during the special, Diana brought out Michael's famously shy side by teasing him in front of the crowd, telling him, "I didn't know you were going to get so sexy." Michael laughed and covered his face, replying, "You're embarrassing me!"

The Look: In a later studio segment shot for the special, the two wore matching white suits over black, heavily sequined shirts a quintessential early-80s, Off the Wall era look.

Another Duet: Aside from "Rock With You" and "Upside Down," the special also featured the two of them singing "Ease On Down the Road" from their 1978 movie The Wiz, accompanied by Quincy Jones on the piano.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE - ROCK WITH YOU 1980
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s notable 1980 performance of "Rock With You" took place at a major charity event designed to raise funds and awareness for a global crisis.

Here are the details of the performance:

The "Because We Care" Gala
Date: January 29, 1980
Event: The "Because We Care" Gala 
Location: The Dorothy Chandler Pavilion in Los Angeles, California (broadcast as a CBS television special).
Cause: The gala was a UNICEF charity event organized to raise funds for Operation USA, specifically providing relief for starving refugees in Cambodia.

Performance Highlights
The Look: Jackson performed wearing a classic, sparkly black tuxedo with a bowtie, perfectly capturing his transition into his *Off the Wall* solo era.
The Audio: As was common for televised award shows and galas of that era, the performance was completely lip-synced to the studio track rather than featuring live vocals, and he danced without a live backing band on stage.

The Speech Following the performance, a visibly shy but sincere Jackson gave a brief, humble speech to the crowd. He said: "Thank you. Thank you very much. Thank you very much, not only for your applause, but thank you for caring; and I'm very happy to be here."

At the time of this performance, "Rock With You" was in the middle of a multi-week run at the #1 spot on the Billboard Hot 100, firmly establishing Jackson as a dominant solo artist outside of The Jacksons.
